To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have proposed an efficient computational approach to modelling surface and interface effects in nanocomposites and to determining the effective elastic properties of the latter.
the developed computational technique can efficiently and accurately compute the overall size dependent effective elastic properties of nanomaterial and nanosized structures.

1) a numerical approach combining the level set and the XFEM is developed to model the size dependent behaviour of nanocomposites and to compute their size dependent effective elastic properties; 2) the developed computational approach is validated and verified by comparing the numerical results with relevant benchmark solutions; 3) the computational approach developed is used to compute the size dependent elastic properties of a nanocomposite consisting of a matrix and nanoinclusions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a computational approach to dealing with surface/interface effects in nanocomposites and to evaluating the effective elastic properties of such materials.
the development of computational techniques to model surface and interface effects in nanocomposites and to determine the effective elastic properties of such materials.
developing a numerical approach to modelling surface and interface effects in nanocomposites and to computing the effective elastic properties of the latter.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the present work has provided a novel and efficient computational tool for the analysis of the size dependent overall elastic behaviour of nanostructured materials.
the developed computational technique is a promising and effective tool for evaluating the size dependent overall elastic behaviour of nanosized structures and nanocomposites.

the present work has provided a computational technique which has the potential to become an efficient tool for dealing with the interface effect in a number of nanostructured materials and for evaluating the size dependent effective behaviour of nanocomposites.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the developed computational technique can accurately and efficiently deal with the interface effects in a nano structured material and determine the size dependent effective moduli of nanomaterial composites.

the developed numerical technique is capable to capture the interface effect on the effective elastic behaviour of nanocomposites, and the results obtained by the present computational approach are in good agreement with the relevant exact solutions.

the developed computational technique is able to capture the size dependent effective moduli of nanomaterial and nano sized structures and that the developed technique is capable of predicting the size dependent effective mechanical behaviour of nanomaterilas and nano structures.

the interface effects are significant and cannot be neglected in nanostructures.
